Questions are answered in assignment order. Questions 1–2 use all posts;
Questions 3–8 analyze posts tagged English.

## Setup: load the data

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(tm)
library(SnowballC)
library(tidytext)
library(wordcloud)
library(ggplot2)

set1 <- read_csv("data/TADA_A1_set1.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
set2 <- read_csv("data/TADA_A1_set2.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

set1$set <- "Set 1"
set2$set <- "Set 2"
tweets <- bind_rows(set1, set2)
```

## 1. What are the date ranges for the two sets? What information is provided in the CSV files? What are the languages in which tweets have been posted?

`location` is profile text, not the post's location.

```{r data-overview}
tweets |>
  group_by(set) |>
  summarise(first_date = min(as.Date(date)),
            last_date = max(as.Date(date)), .groups = "drop")

original_columns <- setdiff(names(set1), "set")
column_types <- vapply(set1[original_columns], function(x) {
  paste(class(x), collapse = "/")
}, character(1))

tibble(
  column = original_columns,
  type = column_types,
  information = c("Identifier supplied with each post", "Date of the post",
                  "Supplied language code", "Post text", "Profile location text")
) |> knitr::kable()
# `set` was added in Setup; it is not an original CSV field.

tweets |>
  count(set, lang) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = set, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(desc(`Set 1` + `Set 2`)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## 2. What is the total number of posts in set 1? What is the total in set 2?

`total_posts` includes all languages; `english_posts` is used in Questions 3–8.

```{r total-posts}
tweets |>
  group_by(set) |>
  summarise(total_posts = n(), english_posts = sum(lang == "en", na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
```

## 3. How many tweets are there for methadone, Suboxone, and fentanyl in total?

Counts are per post and per substance. Categories may overlap; duplicate rows
remain separate observations.

### Step 1: prepare the text

Use English posts. Normalize case and accents; remove links and usernames. Keep
numbers for dose matching.

```{r prepare-text}
substances <- c("methadone", "suboxone", "fentanyl")
english_tweets <- tweets |>
  filter(lang == "en") |>
  mutate(row_id = row_number(), date = as.Date(date))

english_tweets$text <- stringi::stri_trans_general(english_tweets$text, "Latin-ASCII")
english_tweets$text <- tolower(english_tweets$text)
english_tweets$text <- str_remove_all(english_tweets$text, "\\p{Cf}")
english_tweets$text <- gsub("https?://\\S+|www\\.\\S+|@[[:alnum:]_]+",
                            " ", english_tweets$text, perl = TRUE)
english_tweets$text <- gsub("&amp;|&", " and ", english_tweets$text)
english_tweets$text <- gsub("$uboxone", "suboxone", english_tweets$text, fixed = TRUE)
english_tweets$text <- str_squish(english_tweets$text)

whole_word <- function(x) paste0("\\b(?:", x, ")\\b")
```

### Step 2: build the name dictionary

Only listed names and spelling variants count. Fentanyl analogs are counted in
Question 4.

```{r name-lists}
# Count only these listed drug names and variants.
named_drugs <- list(
  methadone = c("methadone", "methadose", "dolophine", "methodone"),
  suboxone = c("suboxone", "suboxon", "suboxen"),
  fentanyl = c("fentanyl", "fentynal", "fentanil")
)
dictionary <- named_drugs

# Keep analogs separate from parent fentanyl; allow spaced and hyphenated names.
analog_patterns <- c(
  methoxyacetylfentanyl = "\\bmethoxyacetyl[ -]?fentan[yi]l\\b",
  carfentanil = "\\b(?:carfentan[yi]l|carfentenil|carefentanyl|carfentayl|carfentantil|carfenta|carfent)\\b",
  acetylfentanyl = "\\b(?:acetyl|acety)[ -]?fentan[yi]l\\b",
  furanylfentanyl = "\\bfuranyl[ -]?fentan[yi]l\\b",
  cyclopropylfentanyl = "\\bcyclopropyl[ -]?fentan[yi]l\\b",
  acrylfentanyl = "\\bacryl[ -]?fentan[yi]l\\b",
  butyrylfentanyl = "\\bbut(?:yryl|yr|iryl)[ -]?fentan[yi]l\\b",
  valerylfentanyl = "\\bvaleryl[ -]?fentan[yi]l\\b",
  benzylfentanyl = "\\bbenzyl[ -]?fentan[yi]l\\b",
  crotonylfentanyl = "\\bcrotonyl[ -]?fentan[yi]l\\b",
  methylfentanyl = "\\b(?:(?:alpha|3)[ -]?)?methyl[ -]?fentan[yi]l\\b",
  fluorofentanyl = "\\b(?:(?:4|para)[ -]?)?fluoro[ -]?fentan[yi]l\\b",
  ocfentanil = "\\bocfentan[yi]l\\b",
  alfentanil = "\\balfentan[yi]l\\b",
  sufentanil = "\\bsufentan[yi]l\\b",
  remifentanil = "\\bremifentan[yi]l\\b"
)
```

Candidate words are one edit from a drug name, or two edits and present in at
least five posts. These are discovery candidates; only variants in the
dictionary above are counted.

```{r spelling-candidates}
# Count a word once per post, then find close spellings of each drug name.
word_rows <- english_tweets |>
  transmute(row_id, word = str_extract_all(text, "\\b[a-z][a-z0-9]{5,10}\\b")) |>
  unnest(word) |>
  distinct(row_id, word)
word_counts <- word_rows |> count(word, name = "posts")

spelling_candidates <- list()
for (seed in substances) {
  candidates <- word_counts |>
    filter(abs(nchar(word) - nchar(seed)) <= 2,
           !word %in% unlist(named_drugs)) |>
    mutate(distance = as.integer(adist(word, seed))) |>
    filter(distance == 1 | (distance == 2 & posts >= 5),
           !word %in% c("methane", "methadrone"),
           !str_detect(word, paste(analog_patterns, collapse = "|"))) |>
    mutate(substance = seed)
  spelling_candidates[[seed]] <- candidates
}
spelling_candidates <- bind_rows(spelling_candidates) |>
  arrange(substance, desc(posts), word)

spelling_candidates |>
  group_by(substance) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(substance, candidate = word, posts, distance) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

### Step 3: match names and hashtags

Expand listed names inside hashtags, then match whole words. Remove analog names
before matching parent fentanyl. Count each post once per substance.

```{r match-hashtags-and-names}
name_patterns <- list()
for (substance in substances) {
  name_patterns[[substance]] <- whole_word(paste(dictionary[[substance]], collapse = "|"))
}
combo_pattern <- "\\bbuprenorphine\\s*(?:[/+-]|and|with)\\s*naloxone\\b"

# Match known compounds first so an analog is not split into parent fentanyl.
other_modified_names <- "(?:nor|despropionyl|ohme|7m)fentan[yi]l"
hashtag_names <- c(other_modified_names,
                   gsub("\\b", "", analog_patterns, fixed = TRUE),
                   unlist(dictionary, use.names = FALSE))
hashtag_pattern <- paste0("(", paste(hashtag_names, collapse = "|"), ")")
expand_hashtag <- function(tags) {
  tags <- gsub("#|_", " ", tags)
  str_replace_all(tags, hashtag_pattern, " \\1 ")
}
english_tweets$text <- str_replace_all(english_tweets$text, "#[a-z0-9_]+", expand_hashtag)
english_tweets$text <- str_squish(english_tweets$text)

parent_text <- str_replace_all(english_tweets$text,
                              paste(analog_patterns, collapse = "|"), " ")
english_tweets <- english_tweets |>
  mutate(methadone = str_detect(text, name_patterns[["methadone"]]),
         suboxone = str_detect(text, name_patterns[["suboxone"]]) |
           str_detect(text, combo_pattern),
         fentanyl = str_detect(parent_text, name_patterns[["fentanyl"]]))

analysis_text <- english_tweets$text
for (analog in names(analog_patterns)) {
  analysis_text <- str_replace_all(analysis_text, analog_patterns[[analog]], analog)
}
for (substance in substances) {
  analysis_text <- str_replace_all(analysis_text, name_patterns[[substance]], substance)
}
analysis_text <- str_replace_all(analysis_text, combo_pattern, "suboxone")
substance_counts <- english_tweets |>
  group_by(set) |>
  summarise(english_posts = n(),
            any_substance = sum(methadone | suboxone | fentanyl),
            across(all_of(substances), ~sum(.x)), .groups = "drop")
substance_counts |> knitr::kable()
english_tweets |>
  summarise(english_posts = n(),
            any_substance = sum(methadone | suboxone | fentanyl),
            across(all_of(substances), ~sum(.x))) |> knitr::kable()
```

## 4. Are there fentanyl analogs that are also being discussed (e.g., carfentanil)?

The reference-based dictionary includes spelling, spacing, and hyphen variants;
additional names were identified by searching the tweet vocabulary for `fent`.
Norfentanyl is excluded. Counts are per post; parent fentanyl and any analog are
reported separately.

```{r analogs}
# One column per analog: TRUE means that its name occurs in the post.
analog_flags <- list()
for (analog in names(analog_patterns)) {
  analog_flags[[analog]] <- str_detect(english_tweets$text, analog_patterns[[analog]])
}
analog_flags <- as.data.frame(analog_flags)
analog_counts <- bind_cols(english_tweets |> select(set), analog_flags) |>
  group_by(set) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(names(analog_patterns)), ~sum(.x)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(-set, names_to = "analog", values_to = "posts")
analog_counts |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = set, values_from = posts) |>
  mutate(total = `Set 1` + `Set 2`) |>
  arrange(desc(total)) |> knitr::kable()

english_tweets$any_analog <- rowSums(analog_flags) > 0
english_tweets |>
  group_by(set) |>
  summarise(parent_fentanyl = sum(fentanyl),
            fentanyl_or_analog = sum(fentanyl | any_analog),
            any_analog = sum(any_analog), .groups = "drop")
```

References: [DEA](https://www.dea.gov/sites/default/files/pr/speeches-testimony/2017t/062717t.pdf),
[US Sentencing Commission](https://www.ussc.gov/research/research-reports/fentanyl-and-fentanyl-analogues-federal-trends-and-trafficking-patterns),
[CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/69/wr/mm6910a4.htm),
[CDC analog list](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/68/wr/mm6834a2.htm),
[acrylfentanyl study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27476446/), and
[FDA review](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/pre96/020630Orig1s000rev.pdf).
This is a focused name search, not an exhaustive inventory or evidence of exposure.

## 5. What are some of the topics that are most closely associated with each of the three substances?

Summarize associated words, common words, and predefined treatment/harm keywords.

### Preprocess the corpus as in Labs 2 and 3

Lowercase, remove punctuation, numbers, and stopwords, then stem and build the
document-term matrix. Keep unstemmed text for drug matching and bigrams.

```{r make-dtm}
# Lab text processing; drug names were normalized in Question 3.
corpus <- Corpus(VectorSource(analysis_text))
corpus <- tm_map(corpus, content_transformer(tolower))
corpus <- tm_map(corpus, removePunctuation)
corpus <- tm_map(corpus, removeNumbers)
myStopWords <- c(stopwords("english"), "rt", "amp")
corpus <- tm_map(corpus, removeWords, myStopWords)
corpus <- tm_map(corpus, stemDocument, language = "english")
corpus <- tm_map(corpus, stripWhitespace)
dtm <- DocumentTermMatrix(corpus)
clean_text <- sapply(corpus, as.character)
```

### Associated and common words

`findAssocs()` reports correlations with stemmed drug names. The top-word table
reports counts and percentages of matched posts (each word counted once per post).

```{r find-associated-terms}
# Prune the sparse association matrix for `findAssocs()`.
association_dtm <- removeSparseTerms(dtm, 0.995)
drug_stems <- wordStem(substances, language = "english")
associations <- findAssocs(association_dtm, drug_stems, 0.1)
names(associations) <- substances
associations

memberships <- english_tweets |>
  select(row_id, set, all_of(substances)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(substances), names_to = "substance", values_to = "mentioned") |>
  filter(mentioned)
substance_sizes <- memberships |> count(substance, name = "matched_posts")

# Remove focal drug stems so the summaries emphasize surrounding content.
cloud_stopwords <- c(drug_stems, "fent")
word_posts <- tibble(row_id = english_tweets$row_id, text = clean_text) |>
  unnest_tokens(word, text) |>
  filter(str_detect(word, "^[a-z]+$"), nchar(word) > 2,
         !word %in% cloud_stopwords) |>
  distinct(row_id, word)
term_rates <- word_posts |>
  inner_join(memberships |> select(row_id, substance), by = "row_id",
             relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  count(substance, word, name = "posts") |>
  left_join(substance_sizes, by = "substance") |>
  mutate(percent = 100 * posts / matched_posts)
top_terms <- term_rates |>
  group_by(substance) |>
  slice_max(posts, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(substance, word, posts, percent)
top_terms |> knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

### Treatment and harm-related topics

Search unstemmed text for the listed keywords. Heatmap values are percentages of
matched posts; categories can overlap and are not model-discovered topics.

```{r theme-vocabulary, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
theme_patterns <- c(
  "Treatment / recovery" = "\\b(treatment|recovery|rehab)\\b",
  "Clinics" = "\\bclinics?\\b",
  "Take-home medication" = "\\btake[ -]?homes?\\b",
  "Prescriptions / pharmacies" = "\\b(prescriptions?|pharmac[yi][[:alpha:]]*)\\b",
  "Cost / insurance" = "\\b(costs?|expensive|afford[[:alpha:]]*|insurance)\\b",
  "Withdrawal" = "\\bwithdrawals?\\b",
  "Overdose" = "\\boverdose[ds]?\\b|\\boverdosing\\b",
  "Contamination / lacing" = "\\b(laced|lacing|contaminat[[:alpha:]]*)\\b"
)
# One yes/no column per keyword category.
theme_flags <- list()
for (topic in names(theme_patterns)) {
  theme_flags[[topic]] <- str_detect(english_tweets$text, theme_patterns[[topic]])
}
theme_flags <- as.data.frame(theme_flags, check.names = FALSE)
theme_rates <- bind_cols(english_tweets |> select(row_id), theme_flags) |>
  pivot_longer(-row_id, names_to = "theme", values_to = "present") |>
  inner_join(memberships |> select(row_id, set, substance), by = "row_id",
             relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  group_by(set, substance, theme) |>
  summarise(posts = sum(present), matched_posts = n(),
            percent = 100 * posts / matched_posts, .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(theme = factor(theme, levels = rev(names(theme_patterns))))

theme_rates |>
  group_by(substance, theme) |>
  summarise(posts = sum(posts), matched_posts = sum(matched_posts),
            percent = 100 * posts / matched_posts, .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(substance) |>
  slice_max(percent, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |> select(substance, theme, posts, percent) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

ggplot(theme_rates, aes(set, theme, fill = percent)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", percent)), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~substance) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f1f5f9", high = "#2878a0", name = "% of posts") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Treatment and harm-related vocabulary",
       subtitle = "Cell values: % of posts mentioning the substance in that set") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## 6. Generate word clouds for each set, so that they can be shown to the researcher.

One cloud per dataset; word size reflects the number of posts containing the word.

```{r word-clouds, fig.height=6, fig.width=8}
set.seed(740)
for (period in c("Set 1", "Set 2")) {
  words <- word_posts |>
    inner_join(english_tweets |> filter(set == period) |> select(row_id),
               by = "row_id") |>
    count(word, sort = TRUE)
  wordcloud(words$word, words$n, max.words = 60, min.freq = 2,
            random.order = FALSE, scale = c(3.5, 0.6))
  title(main = paste(period, "- English posts"))
}
```

## 7. Generate appropriate figures to compare how the frequencies of mentions of these substances differ.

Use percentages of English posts because set sizes differ. Categories can overlap;
the collection periods do not support a clean pre/post-pandemic comparison.

### Mentions by dataset

Bar heights show percentages; labels show the number of matching posts.

```{r compare-sets, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
mention_counts <- substance_counts |>
  select(set, english_posts, all_of(substances)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(substances), names_to = "substance", values_to = "posts") |>
  mutate(percent = 100 * posts / english_posts)
mention_counts

ggplot(mention_counts, aes(substance, percent, fill = set)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = format(posts, big.mark = ",")),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of English posts", title = "Substance mentions by set",
       subtitle = "Labels show post counts; categories can overlap") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Weekly trends

Weekly percentages use each week's English-post count as the denominator.

```{r mentions-over-time, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
# Monday-starting calendar weeks, kept separate across the gap between sets.
weekly_counts <- english_tweets |>
  mutate(week = as.Date(cut(date, "week", start.on.monday = TRUE))) |>
  group_by(set, week) |>
  summarise(english_posts = n(), observed_days = n_distinct(date),
            across(all_of(substances), ~sum(.x)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(substances), names_to = "substance", values_to = "posts") |>
  mutate(percent = 100 * posts / english_posts)
ggplot(weekly_counts, aes(week, percent, group = set)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~substance) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.Date("2020-03-11"), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Week starting Monday", y = "% of English posts that week",
       title = "Weekly substance mentions",
       subtitle = "Dashed line: March 11, 2020; all panels use the same scale") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Dashed line: [WHO pandemic declaration, March 11, 2020](https://www.who.int/news-room/speeches/item/who-director-general-s-opening-remarks-at-the-media-briefing-on-covid-19---11-march-2020).

## 8. Find the top 10 most frequent bigrams in each of the three sets. Plot a bar chart for these.

Find the ten most frequent adjacent word pairs in each substance-matched group.
Pairs containing English stopwords are removed; repeated pairs count repeatedly.

```{r bigrams, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
bigram_counts <- english_tweets |>
  select(row_id, text) |>
  unnest_tokens(bigram, text, token = "ngrams", n = 2) |>
  separate(bigram, into = c("word1", "word2"), sep = " ") |>
  filter(!word1 %in% stopwords("english"),
         !word2 %in% stopwords("english")) |>
  unite(bigram, word1, word2, sep = " ")

top_bigrams <- list()
for (substance in substances) {
  matched_posts <- english_tweets |>
    filter(.data[[substance]]) |>
    select(row_id)
  top10 <- bigram_counts |>
    inner_join(matched_posts, by = "row_id") |>
    count(bigram, sort = TRUE) |>
    slice_head(n = 10)

  top_bigrams[[substance]] <- mutate(top10, substance = substance)
  print(top10)

  print(ggplot(top10, aes(reorder(bigram, n), n)) +
          geom_col() + coord_flip() +
          labs(x = NULL, y = "Count", title = paste("Bigrams:", substance)))
}
```

```{r save-final-results, include=FALSE}
write_csv(analog_counts, "results/analog_counts.csv")
write_csv(top_terms, "results/top_terms.csv")
write_csv(theme_rates, "results/topic_vocabulary.csv")
write_csv(weekly_counts, "results/weekly_mentions.csv")
write_csv(bind_rows(top_bigrams), "results/top_bigrams.csv")
tibble(substance = rep(names(dictionary), lengths(dictionary)),
       term = unlist(dictionary, use.names = FALSE)) |>
  write_csv("results/name_variants.csv")
```
